External native call with no params, mapping to real `IDirect3DQuery9::Issue(DWORD dwIssueFlags)` - the JNI wrapper appears to hardcode the flag (almost certainly D3DISSUE_END, the only flag valid for D3DQUERYTYPE_EVENT) rather than exposing it. Confirmed call site: D3dRenderDevice.kt method3633 (`this.anIDirect3DDevice9810!!.b()` creates the query, then `idirect3deventquery!!.Issue()`), part of a GPU-fence/flush helper: after Issue(), the method spins on IsSignaled() until the GPU catches up, then releases the query. External native call, maps to `IDirect3DQuery9::GetData(NULL, 0, D3DGETDATA_FLUSH)` used with D3DQUERYTYPE_EVENT to poll whether the previously-issued fence has completed. Confirmed call site D3dRenderDevice.kt method3633: `while (true) { val i = idirect3deventquery.IsSignaled(); if (i != 1) break; Thread.yield() }` - the loop spins (yielding the thread) while the result is 1 (matching D3D9's S_FALSE/'still pending' semantics for GetData) and stops once it differs (S_OK/'signaled'), i.e. this implements a blocking wait-for-GPU-idle/flush primitive.
